newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha softer, wet June lot fixed discount.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha softer, wet June lot fixed discount.

text.p: Naphtha prices moved lower in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday in reaction to crudes which fell sharply on the ACCESS after-hours trading system due to a bearish stock build-up in the United States.

Bids for first-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $212.00 per tonne, while offers were assessed at $212.50. In late Tuesday trading, the first-half July contract was bid at $213.50 with no offers having surfaced.
The half-month spread between second-half June and first-half July was discussed at around minus $1.00 after having been traded on Tuesday at minus $1.25.
Also on Tuesday, the first-half June contract was traded between European traders at $211.00.

A major Japanese refiner said it bought one physical cargo to be delivered to Chiba, east of Tokyo, in the latter half of June for its petrochemical affiliate. The price was "slightly lower than the mean of Japanese quotes minus $1.50" per tonne, a trader with the refiner said.
The trader added the firm may need to buy one more spot cargo for first-half June delivery to Kawasaki, near Tokyo, for another petrochemical affiliate of the refiner.
